result:
If I could change the world in one fundamental way, I would abolish the concept of scarcity.

Not just the scarcity of resources (though poverty, hunger, and lack drive so much suffering), but the scarcity of opportunity, recognition, and humanity. A world where limits are artificial and shared abundance is the default—where no child starves because we hoard, no voice is silenced because we fear excess, and no dream is abandoned because it seems unattainable.

This isn’t about utopian fantasy; it’s about dismantling the systems that turn plenty into privilege. It means redefining value beyond accumulation, reallocating power beyond hierarchy, and remembering that our planet provides enough for all if we learn to live within its rhythm rather than against it.

What if we built a world where no one had to fight for survival—not because struggle is erased, but because cooperation eclipses competition?

Then maybe we’d finally have time to ask the deeper questions: *What does it mean to thrive?*
